result.topic_en: The page finishes the table of linear forms 4a·s ± r for the prime divisors of a^m − 1 and a^m + 1 for a = 23 to 30. It then states two theorems: the prime divisors of xx − ayy and of xx + ayy lie in the forms 4as ± T and 4as ± Θ, and these theorems still need proof.

Poftquam pro quouis numero $a$, fiue primo, fiue compofito, valores litterarum T et $\Theta$ fuerint inuenti, fequentia duo theoremata notari merentur.

I. Omnes diuifores primi formae $xx - ayy$ in alterutra harum formarum: $4as + \mathrm{T}$, vel $4as - \mathrm{T}$ continentur.

II. Omnes diuifores primi huius formae: $xx + ayy$ in alteruta harum formularum: $4as + \mathrm{T}$ [?] vel $4as - \Theta$ continentur.

Sponte autem patet pro $x$ et $y$ eiusmodi numeros fumi debere, vt bina membra $xx$ et $ayy$ nullum habeant diuiforem communem.

items.english: In this field nothing else seems to remain except that those two conclusions, deduced from observations, be fortified with firm demonstrations.

items.quote: I. Omnes diuifores primi formae $xx - ayy$ in alterutra harum formarum: $4as + \mathrm{T}$, vel $4as - \mathrm{T}$ continentur.
items.english: I. All prime divisors of the form xx − ayy are contained in one or other of these forms: 4as + T or 4as − T.

items.quote: II. Omnes diuifores primi huius formae: $xx + ayy$ in alteruta harum formularum: $4as + \mathrm{T}$ [?] vel $4as - \Theta$ continentur.
items.english: II. All prime divisors of this form, xx + ayy, are contained in one or other of these formulas: 4as + T [probably Θ] or 4as − Θ.
